item.title: US Job Openings Edged Down in June, Layoffs Remained Limited
item.description: US job openings eased in June but hiring picked up, indicating relatively steady demand for workers heading into the summer.

item.title: Bond Dealers Expect US Will Avoid Signaling Auction Increases
item.description: The US Treasury will need to increase the sizes of at least some of its fixed-rate borrowing programs next year but is unlikely to signal the shift just yet, according to bond dealers.

item.title: Taiwan’s TCC Is Said to Favor London for IPO of European Unit
item.description: Taiwanese conglomerate TCC Group Holdings Co. is leaning toward listing its European operations in London, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest overseas group to be drawn to the UK capital market.

item.title: Ukraine Railway Seeks New Grain Routes as Russia Strikes Ports
item.description: Ukraine’s state rail operator is looking to add new export routes for the country’s critical grain harvest, after Russian attacks on its Black Sea ports curbed shipments.

item.title: Liechtenstein Hunts Hackers as Data on 31,000 Funds Breached
item.description: Liechtenstein is racing to identify the hackers behind a large-scale data breach at the government’s confidential registry of foundations and trusts.

item.title: A Quant and a Korean Dentist Push the Limits of Leveraged ETFs
item.description: A growing number of investors from the US to South Korea are using leveraged exchange-traded funds for long-term investing, a far cry from the day trading they were designed for.

item.title: AbbVie Seeks at Least $8 Billion in Debt to Fund Apogee Deal
item.description: AbbVie Inc. is seeking to raise at least $8 billion from an investment-grade bond offering to fund a portion of its acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics Inc.

item.title: World Bank Urges Emerging Nations to Embrace AI Amid Weak Growth
item.description: Developing economies must move fast in adopting artificial intelligence for their governments and businesses, the World Bank said, urging countries to adapt existing tools to local needs.

item.title: US Trade Deficit Narrows to $73.3 Billion on Drop in Imports
item.description: The US trade deficit narrowed in June as imports fell for the first time since the start of the year in a broad decline.

item.title: Canada Posts Fourth Straight Trade Surplus on Gold Shipments
item.description: Canada’s trade surplus widened slightly in June as an increase in gold exports more than offset a decline in energy shipments.

item.title: India Boosts LIC Share Sale to $3.3 Billion on Strong Demand
item.description: India on Tuesday expanded the size of its share sale in the state-run insurance giant to raise $3.3 billion after the base offer was oversubscribed, bolstering public finances amid challenges posed by high oil prices.

item.title: Bessent Says Yen Level Problem for Japan, Other Currencies
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the weakness of the yen has contributed to Japan’s inflation problem and raised the risk of broader depreciation of Asian currencies as he reiterated US support for efforts to stabilize the situation.

item.title: France, UK to Chair Body Overhauling Zimbabwe’s $23 Billion Debt
item.description: France and the UK agreed to co-chair a body that will help Zimbabwe restructure the billions of dollars it owes creditors, the southern African nation’s Finance Ministry said.

item.title: Fed’s Paulson Says She Keeps ‘Open Mind’ on Interest Rates
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said she will keep an open mind about the path for interest rates, focusing on the trends of underlying inflation.

item.title: Anthropic Inks $10 Billion Computing Deal With Cloud Startup
item.description: Anthropic PBC has struck a $10 billion deal for computing capacity from a months-old infrastructure startup, according to people familiar with the matter, marking the Claude maker’s latest effort to keep pace with demand for its products.

item.title: CoreWeave to Enter Asian Market With Indonesian Data Centers
item.description: AI cloud company CoreWeave Inc. is entering the Asian market with its first data centers in the region, expanding to a rapidly growing part of the world that is clamoring for more computing power.

item.title: India Panel Proposes Rules to Bring Overseas Firms Home
item.description: A panel of Indian lawmakers has proposed allowing companies registered overseas to transfer their registration to an International Financial Services Centre in India.

item.title: Bending Spoons to Buy Software Firm Airtable For $2.3 Billion
item.description: App developer Bending Spoons SpA has agreed to buy software firm Airtable for an equity value of $2.25 billion, a sharp decline from the startup’s 2021 peak valuation.

item.title: India’s New Closing Auction Sparks Second Nifty Jump on Expiry
item.description: India’s first weekly derivatives expiry under the new closing auction system did little to ease concerns about the new mechanism after the benchmark NSE Nifty 50 Index again moved sharply during the auction, after surprising traders on Monday.

item.title: Bridgepoint Explores €1 Billion Private Credit Secondaries Deal
item.description: Bridgepoint Group is exploring a deal to sell more than €1 billion ($1.15 billion) of private credit stakes in a secondaries transaction, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.description: Oracle Corp. and Stellantis NV are among a group of high-grade companies with debt that has recently traded close to junk levels, putting the bond market on watch for a new era of fallen angels.

item.title: Emerging Markets Stay Under Pressure as Iran Impasse Lifts Oil
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies stayed under pressure as the lack of progress on US-Iran talks lifted oil prices back above $86 a barrel.
